title: Kathmandu → Pokhara
distance: 200 km · Prithvi Highway or 25 min by air
summary: The classic Nepal hop: out of the valley, along the Trishuli, into the lake basin under Machhapuchhre. Choose the highway if you want the river and tea stalls; fly if you want the same afternoon on Phewa.

alongTheWay.name: Thankot ridge
alongTheWay.do: Last valley view, buy water, then the road drops to the Trishuli.
alongTheWay.detail: The hop leaves the Kathmandu bowl here. Stretch if the driver will wait. After this the highway is river, dust, and tea stalls.
alongTheWay.fact: Thankot was the first ridge the old Tribhuvan Highway crossed when Nepal opened motor roads to India in the 1950s.

alongTheWay.name: Malekhu fish & tea
alongTheWay.do: Eat river fish, chiya, and use a proper toilet.
alongTheWay.detail: Most tourist buses pause here. It is the civilised lunch of the KTM–Pokhara road — not a tourist attraction, just the right stop.
alongTheWay.fact: Malekhu is famous for masula — small river fish fried whole — served with dal bhat to thousands of highway travellers every day.

alongTheWay.name: Trishuli riverside
alongTheWay.do: Half-day raft, then continue to Pokhara by waiting jeep or your own car.
alongTheWay.detail: Put-ins sit just off the highway. Worth it if you are in a private car and not racing a same-day ABC start. Buses will not wait.
alongTheWay.fact: The Trishuli is one of Nepal’s busiest rafting rivers — grade III–IV in season, fed by Himalayan snowmelt from Langtang and Ganesh Himal.

alongTheWay.name: Manakamana cable car
alongTheWay.do: Ride the cable car, temple, views, then back to the highway.
alongTheWay.detail: Private cars and some jeeps can peel off. A real “something to do between” if you have daylight and are not on a tourist bus clock.
alongTheWay.fact: Manakamana’s cable car was Nepal’s first, opened in 1998 — the temple is a wish-fulfilment shrine where devotees leave bells and coconuts.

alongTheWay.name: Mugling junction
alongTheWay.do: Fuel, chiya, last stretch before the climb into Pokhara.
alongTheWay.detail: Chitwan peels south from here. If Pokhara is the destination, stay on the westbound road.
alongTheWay.fact: Mugling is where three major highways meet — west to Pokhara, south to Chitwan, and east back to Kathmandu — making it Nepal’s busiest road fork.

atDestination.name: Phewa Lake boat
atDestination.detail: Row or hire a boat to Tal Barahi. Late afternoon light is the point.
atDestination.fact: Tal Barahi is a Hindu shrine on a tiny island — locals say the goddess protects Pokhara from floods in the Seti gorge.

atDestination.name: Sarangkot sunrise
atDestination.detail: Machhapuchhre and Annapurna from the ridge. Leave Lakeside before 5:00 in peak season.
atDestination.fact: Machhapuchhre — Fishtail — has never been summited; Nepal bans climbing it as a sacred peak.

atDestination.name: Paragliding
atDestination.detail: From Sarangkot over the lake. Weather and wind cancel — keep a buffer day.
atDestination.fact: Pokhara is one of the world’s top paragliding spots — thermals from Phewa lift pilots above 2,500 m with Annapurna as backdrop.

atDestination.name: World Peace Pagoda
atDestination.detail: Fishtail views and a quiet walk. Good the afternoon you arrive.
atDestination.fact: The Shanti Stupa was built by Japanese monks in 1999 — one of eighty peace pagodas worldwide, all meant to spread non-violence.

atDestination.name: Lakeside evening
atDestination.detail: Eat, sort ABC permits if you continue, sleep early. Jeeps leave 7:00–8:00.
atDestination.fact: Lakeside was a hippie trail stop in the 1970s — today it is still where trekkers buy permits, rent gear, and book jeeps to Nayapul.

modes.name: Tourist bus
modes.from: Thamel / Kantipath hotel pickup or tourist bus park
modes.detail: AC or fan coaches (Greenline, Golden, similar). One long lunch stop, reclining seats, luggage in the hold. Morning departures around 7:00. Buy the day before in high season.
extras: Hotel pickup on some tickets · NPR 0–300
modes.goodFor: Solo travellers, scenery, daylight highway

modes.name: Micro / local bus
modes.to: Pokhara bus park, then taxi to Lakeside ~NPR 400–700
modes.detail: Faster when traffic is kind, slower when it is not. No hotel pickup, tighter seats, more stops. Fine if you speak a little Nepali and want the local road.
modes.goodFor: Tight budgets, flexible departure

modes.name: Private car / jeep
modes.detail: Toyota or similar, up to 3–4 passengers with bags. Stop where you want: Malekhu, rafting, Manakamana, photos. Best if you are a pair or small family and want the hop to feel like the trip.
extras: Manakamana detour · extra 2–3 hrs + cable car tickets
modes.goodFor: 2–4 people, stops, children, extra luggage

modes.name: Domestic flight
modes.duration: 20 – 25 minutes flying · 2–3 hrs airport to hotel
modes.detail: Buddha Air, Yeti, Shree — several frequencies most days. Fares jump at Dashain, Tihar, and autumn trekking season. Mountain views on the right side flying west. Always keep a bus backup in case of fog.
modes.goodFor: Short time, connecting to ABC the next morning

notes: Sample fares for 2026, one way, per person unless noted. Highway time swings with landslides and Dashain traffic. Carry water, cash, and a layer — the valley is warm, the lake can be cool.

title: Pokhara → Annapurna Base Camp
distance: Trailhead 1.5–3.5 hrs · then 4–7 walking days up
summary: Leave Lakeside by jeep or taxi, then walk. The hop is villages, stone stairs, bamboo, and a high sanctuary — not a single vehicle. You can shorten the walk with a jeep to Ghandruk or Chhomrong, or fly out by helicopter if weather and budget allow.

alongTheWay.name: Nayapul / Birethanti
alongTheWay.do: Permit check, chiya, then walk toward Ghandruk or Jhinu.
alongTheWay.detail: Shared jeeps dump you here. Private jeeps can continue higher. This is where the road hop ends and the walking hop begins.
alongTheWay.fact: Birethanti is where the Modi Khola meets the Bhurungdi — trekkers cross the same suspension bridge that appears on countless ABC postcards.

alongTheWay.name: Ghandruk
alongTheWay.do: Gurung Museum, terraces, Machhapuchhre in the window.
alongTheWay.detail: A jeep here cuts a dusty lower day. Stay the night if you arrived late. Stone village, not a checkpoint.
alongTheWay.fact: Ghandruk is one of Nepal’s largest Gurung villages — stone houses stacked on terraces with Machhapuchhre framed in every window.

alongTheWay.name: Jhinu Danda hot springs
alongTheWay.when: On the Chhomrong climb or descent
alongTheWay.cost: Small pool fee · extra walking hour
alongTheWay.do: Soak in the Modi Khola pools. Daylight only. Towel from the lodge.
alongTheWay.detail: The thing most people remember between the hard days. Worth the extra stairs on the way down.
alongTheWay.fact: The natural pools sit beside the Modi Khola at about 1,780 m — the water is geothermally heated and locals have soaked here for generations.

alongTheWay.name: Chhomrong · Bamboo · Deurali
alongTheWay.do: Slow stairs, forest, dal bhat, early nights.
alongTheWay.detail: This is the hop — not a transfer. Sleep where the day ends. Water, snacks, and a headtorch matter more than speed.
alongTheWay.fact: Bamboo marks the start of true rhododendron forest — in spring the trail turns crimson and pink under Annapurna South.

alongTheWay.name: Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC)
alongTheWay.do: Walk slow, sleep, leave before dawn for ABC.
alongTheWay.detail: ABC is 1.5–2 hrs further. Do not rush this night. The sanctuary is the next morning.
alongTheWay.fact: MBC sits at 3,700 m directly below Machhapuchhre’s south face — climbers use it as a staging camp, though the peak itself remains forbidden.

atDestination.name: Sunrise at ABC
atDestination.detail: Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, Fishtail. This is the reason for the hop.
atDestination.fact: ABC sits inside a glacial amphitheatre at 4,130 m — Annapurna I (8,091 m) rises just 34 km away, one of the steepest vertical rises on Earth.

atDestination.name: Sanctuary walk
atDestination.detail: Moraine and back to MBC the same morning if you are fit. Then descend.
atDestination.fact: The Annapurna Sanctuary was closed to foreigners until 1956 — the name comes from the ring of peaks that wall off the cirque like a temple.

atDestination.name: Helicopter out
atDestination.detail: Weather window only. Keep walking legs in the plan. Book from Pokhara or by radio in peak season.
atDestination.fact: Heli evacuations from ABC became common after the 2015 earthquake — demand peaks in October when fog still cancels many Pokhara flights.

atDestination.name: Jhinu + Ghandruk on the way down
atDestination.price: Lodge + food as on the way up
atDestination.detail: Hot springs, extra village night, or add a Poon Hill / Ghorepani loop if you have days.
atDestination.fact: Poon Hill (3,210 m) adds two days but rewards you with a 360° panorama of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna — the most photographed sunrise in Nepal.

modes.name: Taxi or jeep to Nayapul, then trek
modes.to: Nayapul / Birethanti, then on foot to ABC
modes.detail: The standard start. Shared jeep in the morning from Lakeside or Baglung bus park. Private jeep if you are a group or starting late. Then walk Ghandruk or New Bridge → Chhomrong → ABC.
extras: Guide / porter if hired in Pokhara
modes.goodFor: Full trail, villages, budget

modes.name: Jeep to Ghandruk or Chhomrong, then trek
modes.to: Ghandruk, Kimche, Siwai or near Chhomrong
modes.detail: Skips the dusty lower road walk. Sleep Ghandruk the first night, or push toward Chhomrong if you jeep to Siwai. Road can close in monsoon or heavy snow — always have a Nayapul backup.
extras: Porter from Ghandruk if you did not hire in Pokhara
modes.goodFor: Limited days, knees, late-season road access

modes.name: Guided ABC package
modes.detail: Guide, permits, lodges, and usually trailhead transfer. Food is often “pay as you go” in tea houses unless the quote says full board. Confirm whether porters, sleeping bag, and down jacket are in. Sample 8-day shape: Pokhara–Ghandruk–Chhomrong–Dovan–MBC–ABC–Jhinu–Pokhara.
extras: Meals NPR 4,000–7,000 / day at higher lodges
modes.goodFor: First Himalayan trek, solo travellers, fixed dates

modes.name: Independent trek + day rates
modes.detail: Lodge NPR 500–2,000 (often waived or cheap if you eat there). Dal bhat and drinks climb with altitude. Guide NPR 2,500–3,500/day if you hire one. Nepali trekkers pay a lower ACAP fee; foreigners need ACAP + TIMS. Carry cash — no reliable ATMs after Pokhara.
includes: You book lodges as you go
extras: TIMS: NPR 2,000 independent / NPR 1,000 via agency (foreigners)
modes.goodFor: Experienced walkers, Nepali groups, open schedule

modes.name: Helicopter ABC → Pokhara
modes.price: US$500 – 1,200 pp shared · charter much higher
modes.detail: Not a guaranteed hop. Cloud, wind, and demand decide. Shared seats are sold in Pokhara or by radio from ABC in peak season. Keep walking legs in the plan. One-way down is the usual use; flying both ways is a luxury sightseeing hop.
extras: Still need permits if you walked in
modes.goodFor: Tight international flights, knee issues on descent

notes: ABC sits at about 4,130 m. Walk slowly from Chhomrong up. Sample prices for 2026; tea-house menus and jeep fares move with fuel and season. Monsoon (Jun–Sep) means leeches, landslides, and closed high lodges some years.

title: Kathmandu → Annapurna Base Camp
distance: Fly or drive to Pokhara, then the sanctuary trail
summary: Two hops stacked: Kathmandu to Pokhara (road or air), then Pokhara to ABC on foot. Do not try to “reach ABC from Kathmandu in a day.” Sleep in Pokhara, sort permits and a guide, start the trail the next morning.

alongTheWay.name: Kathmandu → Pokhara
alongTheWay.do: Arrive Lakeside with daylight if you can.
alongTheWay.detail: Same modes as the Kathmandu–Pokhara hop. Do not try to start the ABC trail the same afternoon unless you flew early and already have permits.
alongTheWay.fact: The KTM–PKR sector is one of the world’s busiest mountain flights — Buddha Air alone runs dozens of daily hops in peak trekking season.

alongTheWay.name: Pokhara night
alongTheWay.do: ATM, permits, sleeping bag, snacks, early dinner.
alongTheWay.detail: Most trailhead jeeps leave 7:00–8:00. This night is part of the hop, not wasted time.
alongTheWay.fact: Pokhara has Nepal’s last reliable ATMs before the trail — after Nayapul, cash only for permits, lodges, and dal bhat.

alongTheWay.name: Trail to ABC
alongTheWay.cost: From NPR 6,000 / day or a package from NPR 55,000
alongTheWay.do: Ghandruk, Chhomrong, Bamboo, Deurali, MBC, ABC, Jhinu down.
alongTheWay.detail: See the Pokhara → ABC hop for every walking mode, permit, and tea-house rate. That is the second road in this stack.
alongTheWay.fact: The full KTM–ABC stack crosses three climate zones in a week — subtropical valley, temperate forest, and alpine sanctuary above 4,000 m.

atDestination.name: Sanctuary sunrise
atDestination.detail: Full cirque, then descend or heli to Pokhara.
atDestination.fact: On a clear morning you can see four peaks above 8,000 m from ABC — a view fewer than 100,000 trekkers reach each year.

atDestination.name: Buffer night in Pokhara
atDestination.detail: Fog cancels KTM–PKR often. Do not book an international flight the same morning you leave ABC.
atDestination.fact: Pokhara airport sits in a bowl — morning fog from Phewa can linger until 10:00, grounding every Kathmandu-bound flight at once.

atDestination.name: Jhinu, Ghandruk, optional Poon Hill
atDestination.detail: Same as the Pokhara–ABC hop. Add days if knees and calendar allow.
atDestination.fact: Most trekkers descend faster than they climb — the same trail feels half the distance on the way down with gravity and hot springs waiting.

modes.name: Fly to Pokhara, then ABC trek
modes.detail: Morning flight, afternoon gear and permits, next-day jeep to the trail. Fastest clean version of Kathmandu to ABC. Keep one buffer day before any international departure.
includes: See KTM–PKR flight + PKR–ABC package / independent rates
modes.goodFor: International visitors, tight calendars

modes.name: Tourist bus to Pokhara, then ABC trek
modes.detail: Leave KTM ~7:00, Lakeside by late afternoon. Same trail as everyone else the next morning. Cheapest full Kathmandu-to-ABC shape that still feels civilised.
extras: Private car instead of bus NPR 14,000–18,000 for the first leg
modes.goodFor: Budget, scenery, no airport gamble

modes.name: Kathmandu-start ABC package
modes.detail: Agency handles KTM hotel pickup, tourist bus or flight, Pokhara night, guide, permits, trail, and return. Ask what is not in: bottled water, hot showers, Wi-Fi, porter, and the Pokhara–KTM flight home. Sample prices; private rooms and peak October cost more.
extras: KTM–PKR flights both ways if you upgrade
modes.goodFor: Landing in KTM and not wanting to stitch it yourself

notes: Kathmandu to ABC is never one vehicle. Price the two legs separately if you like control; buy a package if you want one number. Sample 2026 fares.

title: Kathmandu → Lumbini
distance: 280 km · Prithvi Highway to Mugling, then south via Narayangarh & Butwal
duration: 8 – 10 hours by road · 35 min by air to Bhairahawa
bestSeason: October–March (cooler Terai) · November–February for pilgrimage festivals
summary: The pilgrimage hop: out of the Kathmandu valley, fork south at Mugling, cross the Terai through Chitwan country, and arrive at the Maya Devi garden where Siddhartha Gautama was born. Highway if you want the full road; fly to Bhairahawa if you want the same afternoon at the monasteries.

alongTheWay.name: Thankot ridge
alongTheWay.do: Last valley view, then the road drops toward the Trishuli.
alongTheWay.detail: Same first stretch as the Pokhara hop — the valley ends here. Stretch, buy water, and settle in for a long Terai day.
alongTheWay.fact: From Thankot the road descends 600 m in under an hour — the same drop that made early buses overheat on the way to the plains.

alongTheWay.name: Mugling junction
alongTheWay.do: Turn south toward Narayangarh and Chitwan — not west to Pokhara.
alongTheWay.detail: This is the turn that changes the hop. South from Mugling the road follows the Narayani valley toward the Terai.
alongTheWay.fact: Mugling sits at the confluence of the Trishuli and Marshyangdi — two Himalayan rivers that merge before cutting south to Chitwan.

alongTheWay.name: Narayangarh (Bharatpur)
alongTheWay.do: Eat, stretch, optional quick look at the Narayani riverfront.
alongTheWay.detail: Commercial hub of Chitwan district. Most buses pause here. Chitwan National Park is a short detour east if you add a night.
alongTheWay.fact: Narayangarh is the gateway to Chitwan National Park — home to roughly 600 one-horned rhinos and Bengal tigers you can spot on a jeep safari.

alongTheWay.name: Butwal
alongTheWay.do: Fuel stop, last proper town before Bhairahawa and Lumbini.
alongTheWay.detail: Flat, warm, busy — the Terai feels different here. Lumbini is less than an hour further west.
alongTheWay.fact: Butwal marks the start of the Siddhartha Highway — named for Prince Siddhartha — linking the Indian border at Sunauli to Pokhara via Tansen.

alongTheWay.name: Bhairahawa (Siddharthanagar)
alongTheWay.duration: Taxi 20–30 min to the sacred garden
alongTheWay.do: Fly here if you skipped the highway; taxi or rickshaw to the monastic zone.
alongTheWay.detail: Gautam Buddha Airport (BWA) serves daily flights from Kathmandu. The Lumbini zone is a short hop west — not walkable with luggage in the Terai heat.
alongTheWay.fact: Bhairahawa was renamed Siddharthanagar in honour of the Buddha — the airport code BWA still points pilots to the birthplace hop.

alongTheWay.name: Lumbini monastic zone
alongTheWay.do: Maya Devi Temple, eternal flame, then walk the east or west monastic lanes.
alongTheWay.detail: UNESCO World Heritage site. Flat, hot, contemplative — plan dawn or dusk for the Maya Devi garden and midday shade for the monastery circuit.
alongTheWay.fact: Emperor Ashoka erected a pillar here in 249 BCE marking the Buddha’s birthplace — it still stands beside the Maya Devi Temple.

atDestination.name: Maya Devi Temple
atDestination.detail: The exact spot of the Buddha’s birth — a simple shrine over archaeological ruins, quieter at opening time.
atDestination.fact: Excavations uncovered a marker stone from the 3rd century BCE pinpointing the birth spot — one of the oldest authenticated Buddhist sites on Earth.

atDestination.name: World monasteries walk
atDestination.detail: Thai, Chinese, Korean, German, and Vietnamese temples — each nation built its own interpretation of the sacred garden.
atDestination.fact: Lumbini hosts monasteries from more than twenty countries — a rare place where Thai gold, Tibetan murals, and French modernism sit side by side.

atDestination.name: World Peace Pagoda
atDestination.detail: Cycle or rickshaw north of the canal. Wide Terai views and a calm counterpoint to the Maya Devi crowds.
atDestination.fact: The Lumbini Peace Pagoda was funded by Japanese Buddhists — one of a global network of eighty stupas dedicated to non-violence.

atDestination.name: Crane sanctuary
atDestination.detail: Sarus cranes and wetland birds in the fields around the zone. Best early before the Terai heat.
atDestination.fact: The Sarus crane — the world’s tallest flying bird — nests in Lumbini’s wetlands and features in Buddhist art as a symbol of devotion.

atDestination.name: Eternal flame & evening aarti
atDestination.detail: The flame has burned since 1986 when international pilgrims lit it for world peace. Quiet end to a pilgrimage day.
atDestination.fact: The eternal flame was lit by representatives from twelve nations — one flame, three decades, never extinguished.

modes.name: Tourist / express bus
modes.from: Kalanki or Gongabu bus park, Kathmandu
modes.to: Lumbini bazaar or Sunauli road junction
modes.detail: Direct or semi-direct coaches via Mugling and Butwal. One long day on the road — leave early (6:00–7:00), arrive before dark. Reclining seats on tourist lines; local expresses are cheaper and slower.
includes: One meal stop at Narayangarh or similar
extras: Taxi bazaar to monastic zone NPR 200–400
modes.goodFor: Pilgrims, budget travellers, seeing the full Terai crossing

modes.name: Local bus
modes.detail: More stops, tighter seats, frequent pauses for passengers and cargo. Fine if you speak a little Nepali and are not racing a festival crowd.
extras: Taxi or rickshaw to Maya Devi zone
modes.goodFor: Tight budgets, flexible schedule

modes.name: Private car / jeep
modes.detail: Toyota or similar, up to 3–4 passengers. Stop at Mugling, Narayangarh lunch, or peel off for a half-day Chitwan safari if you add a night. Best for families and pilgrimage groups who want shade and pace control.
modes.goodFor: 2–4 people, Chitwan combo, elders, pilgrimage groups

modes.name: Flight to Bhairahawa
modes.duration: 25 min flying · 1.5 hrs airport to Maya Devi
modes.to: Gautam Buddha Airport (BWA), then taxi to Lumbini
modes.detail: Buddha Air, Yeti, and others fly daily. Terai heat and monsoon haze cancel less often than mountain routes, but still keep a bus backup in peak festival weeks. Taxi to the monastic zone takes 20–30 minutes.
modes.goodFor: Short time, elderly pilgrims, combining with India border crossing at Sunauli

notes: Sample fares for 2026, one way. The Terai is hot March–June — carry water, hat, and light cotton. Lumbini entry is separate from transport; monasteries are free once inside. Sunauli border (India) is 30 min south if you continue overland.

title: Kathmandu → Chitwan
distance: 160 km · Prithvi Highway to Mugling, then south to Sauraha
duration: 5 – 7 hours by road · 20 min by air to Bharatpur
summary: The classic wildlife hop: drop out of the Kathmandu valley, turn south at Mugling, and reach the Terai lodges of Sauraha in one day. Highway for the full road; fly to Bharatpur if you want a jeep safari the same afternoon.

alongTheWay.name: Thankot ridge
alongTheWay.do: Last valley view, then descend toward the Trishuli.
alongTheWay.detail: Same opening stretch as the Pokhara and Lumbini hops — the valley ends quickly and the road warms up.
alongTheWay.fact: Thankot sits at 1,400 m — within an hour you will be near sea-level heat in the Chitwan basin.

alongTheWay.name: Mugling junction
alongTheWay.do: Turn south toward Narayangarh — not west to Pokhara.
alongTheWay.detail: The hop hinges here. Southbound traffic peels off toward Chitwan and the Terai.
alongTheWay.fact: Mugling is where trekkers heading west and safari-goers heading south split — the busiest fork in Nepal.

alongTheWay.name: Kurintar riverside
alongTheWay.do: Raft the Trishuli, then continue south by waiting jeep.
alongTheWay.detail: Only works with a private car or flexible schedule. Tourist buses to Chitwan will not wait.
alongTheWay.fact: Kurintar put-ins sit where the Trishuli cuts through a tight gorge — white water before the plains.

alongTheWay.name: Narayangarh (Bharatpur)
alongTheWay.do: Eat, ATM, then the short hop east to Sauraha.
alongTheWay.detail: Most coaches stop here. Chitwan lodges are 20–30 minutes further by taxi or lodge pickup.
alongTheWay.fact: Bharatpur airport (BHR) receives daily flights from Kathmandu — the fastest way to a rhino safari.

alongTheWay.name: Sauraha & the Rapti
alongTheWay.cost: Park entry NPR 2,000+ · safari from NPR 3,500
alongTheWay.do: Check in, book tomorrow’s jeep safari, sunset by the river.
alongTheWay.detail: Sauraha is the main lodge strip. Book safaris through your hotel or a licensed operator — not touts at the bus stop.
alongTheWay.fact: Chitwan National Park was Nepal’s first national park (1973) and a UNESCO site since 1984.

atDestination.name: Jeep safari
atDestination.time: Half day · dawn or dusk best
atDestination.detail: Rhino, deer, monkeys, and birds from an open jeep. Tiger sightings are luck — ask for the buffer-zone route if the park is crowded.
atDestination.fact: Roughly 600 one-horned rhinos live in Chitwan — one of the largest populations outside India.

atDestination.name: Rapti canoe
atDestination.detail: Quiet paddle for kingfishers, egrets, and mugger crocodiles on the bank. Morning light is cooler and better for photos.
atDestination.fact: The gharial — a fish-eating crocodile with a long narrow snout — breeds in Chitwan and is critically endangered worldwide.

atDestination.name: Tharu village & culture show
atDestination.price: NPR 500 – 1,200 show · village walk often free
atDestination.detail: Traditional stick dance and a short village walk. Good the night you arrive if you came by bus.
atDestination.fact: The Tharu people have lived in the Terai for centuries — many villages resisted malaria when the hills were more populated.

atDestination.name: Elephant breeding centre
atDestination.detail: Government centre near Sauraha. Ethical alternative to riding — observe calves and adults from the path.
atDestination.fact: Elephant rides are phased out in many lodges — the breeding centre focuses on conservation and research.

modes.name: Tourist / express bus
modes.to: Sauraha bus park or lodge pickup
modes.detail: Daily coaches via Mugling to Narayangarh, then branch to Sauraha. Some tickets include lodge pickup — ask when you buy. Leave early for an afternoon check-in.
modes.goodFor: Budget travellers, first safari, seeing the Terai crossing

modes.name: Private car / jeep
modes.detail: Stop at Mugling for tea, Kurintar for rafting if you build in time, or Narayangarh for lunch. Best for families who want AC and pace control.
modes.goodFor: 2–4 people, kids, Kurintar rafting combo

modes.name: Flight to Bharatpur
modes.to: Bharatpur airport, then taxi or lodge pickup to Sauraha
modes.detail: Several flights daily in season. Less fog-prone than mountain routes. Lodge pickup can be pre-arranged — saves haggling at the airport.
modes.goodFor: Short trips, same-day safari booking, avoiding long bus

modes.name: KTM–Chitwan safari package
modes.detail: Bus or flight, lodge, meals, one jeep safari, and canoe often bundled. Confirm what is extra: park fees, tips, drinks, and second safari.
modes.goodFor: First-time visitors who want one price

notes: Sample 2026 fares, one way unless noted. Park fees and safari prices change — confirm at booking. Monsoon (Jun–Sep) means heat, leeches on walks, and occasional road delays.

title: Chitwan → Pokhara
distance: 150 km · East to Mugling, then west on Prithvi Highway
summary: The classic triangle leg: leave the rhinos behind, cut back north through Narayangarh and Mugling, then climb the Prithvi Highway into Pokhara and the Annapurna views. One long day on the road — most travellers stop one night in Chitwan before this hop.

alongTheWay.name: Sauraha to Narayangarh
alongTheWay.cost: NPR 1,200 – 2,000 taxi · lodge pickup often included
alongTheWay.do: Checkout early, reach the highway junction before midday heat.
alongTheWay.detail: Your lodge can arrange the transfer. Shared jeeps exist but are slower — taxi is easier with luggage.
alongTheWay.fact: Sauraha sits on the Rapti river buffer zone — the drive to Narayangarh crosses flat rice fields that flood in monsoon.

alongTheWay.name: Narayangarh lunch stop
alongTheWay.do: Eat, ATM if you need cash for Pokhara.
alongTheWay.detail: Last big town before the highway climb. Good dal bhat before the winding road west.
alongTheWay.fact: Narayangarh grew as a railway and highway hub — it is still the supply town for all of central Chitwan.

alongTheWay.name: Mugling junction
alongTheWay.do: Turn west toward Pokhara — not south or east.
alongTheWay.detail: Buses pause for fuel and tea. After this the road follows the Marsyangdi and Trishuli valleys west.
alongTheWay.fact: From Mugling west, every tourist bus to Pokhara follows the same river corridor trekkers know from the Annapurna approach.

alongTheWay.name: Malekhu fish stop
alongTheWay.do: Optional lunch — river fish and chiya.
alongTheWay.detail: Same stop as the Kathmandu–Pokhara hop. Tourist coaches often break here.
alongTheWay.fact: Malekhu’s fried river fish has been a highway ritual since the Prithvi road opened — drivers know the best stalls.

alongTheWay.name: Pokhara lakeside arrival
alongTheWay.do: Drop bags, walk Phewa if light holds, sort ABC permits if you continue.
alongTheWay.detail: Most buses end at the tourist bus park — taxi to Lakeside NPR 400–700. You should arrive with enough light to find your hotel.
alongTheWay.fact: Pokhara sits at 822 m — after Chitwan’s heat, the lake air feels noticeably cooler.

atDestination.name: Phewa Lake evening
atDestination.detail: Gentle first evening after the long drive. Tal Barahi shrine at dusk if the light is good.
atDestination.fact: Phewa is Nepal’s second-largest lake — the water level drops in dry season, exposing new shoreline paths.

atDestination.name: Sarangkot sunrise
atDestination.detail: Book a taxi the night before. Machhapuchhre and Annapurna from the ridge — worth it before ABC if you continue.
atDestination.fact: Sarangkot is also Nepal’s main paragliding launch — tandem flights run most clear mornings.

atDestination.name: Gear & permit run
atDestination.detail: Thamel-style shops on Lakeside. Get ACAP, TIMS, sleeping bag, and snacks before the jeep to Nayapul.
atDestination.fact: Pokhara issues most Annapurna permits — the ACAP check at Nayapul is faster if paperwork is done here.

modes.name: Tourist bus via Mugling
modes.detail: Some operators run through-services; otherwise taxi to Narayangarh and change to a westbound Pokhara bus. Ask your lodge the night before.
modes.goodFor: Budget, standard triangle route

modes.name: Private car / jeep
modes.detail: One vehicle, stops when you want. Malekhu lunch, photos at Mugling, straight to Lakeside. Best after a early checkout.
extras: Manakamana detour +2–3 hrs if you have time
modes.goodFor: 2–4 people, luggage, families

modes.name: Local bus
modes.detail: Taxi to the highway first. Local buses are frequent Mugling–Pokhara but tighter and slower. Fine if you are not in a rush.
modes.goodFor: Very tight budgets

notes: Sample 2026 fares. The Chitwan–Pokhara hop is one long driving day — do not plan a same-night ABC trail start unless you pre-arranged a dawn jeep. Many travellers do KTM → Chitwan → Pokhara → ABC in sequence.

title: Pokhara → Lumbini
distance: 180 km · Siddhartha Highway via Tansen & Butwal
summary: Cross the mid-hills on the Siddhartha Highway — Palpa ridges, Butwal on the Terai, then the Maya Devi garden. No mountain flight on this hop; it is a full day of winding road and flat heat at the end.

alongTheWay.name: Pokhara valley exit
alongTheWay.do: Leave Lakeside early — 7:00 is ideal.
alongTheWay.detail: The road climbs out of the lake basin toward Kushma and the highway proper. Morning views back to Fishtail if the sky is clear.
alongTheWay.fact: The Siddhartha Highway is named for Prince Siddhartha — it links Pokhara to Lumbini and the Sunauli India border.

alongTheWay.name: Kushma / Kaligandaki gorge
alongTheWay.do: Look down into the Kaligandaki — one of the world’s deepest river gorges.
alongTheWay.detail: Optional pause if you are in a private car. Buses roll through without stopping.
alongTheWay.fact: The Kaligandaki river cuts between Dhaulagiri and Annapurna — sacred stones called shaligram are found in its bed.

alongTheWay.name: Tansen (Palpa)
alongTheWay.do: Walk Srinagar hill for Himalayan views, lunch in the old bazaar.
alongTheWay.detail: A worthwhile detour in a private car. Tourist buses usually skip it — you pass the turn above the ridge.
alongTheWay.fact: Tansen’s Palpa Durbar and Srinagar ridge offer Dhaulagiri and Annapurna views on clear days — a hidden hill town.

alongTheWay.name: Butwal
alongTheWay.do: Fuel, toilet, last town before Bhairahawa and Lumbini.
alongTheWay.detail: The road flattens and warms. Lumbini is less than an hour west.
alongTheWay.fact: Butwal exploded as a trade hub once the Siddhartha Highway connected the hills to the Indian border.

alongTheWay.name: Bhairahawa & Lumbini zone
alongTheWay.do: Check in near the monastic zone; Maya Devi at opening next morning.
alongTheWay.detail: Most buses stop at Lumbini bazaar or Bhairahawa — not at the temple gate. Plan a taxi or rickshaw for the last stretch.
alongTheWay.fact: Gautam Buddha Airport in Bhairahawa also serves pilgrims flying in from Kathmandu — road and air meet here.

atDestination.name: Maya Devi Temple
atDestination.detail: Quieter at opening. The birth-marker stone and Ashoka pillar are the core of the site.
atDestination.fact: UNESCO listed Lumbini in 1997 — the master plan zones monasteries by country east and west of the canal.

atDestination.name: Monastic zone circuit
atDestination.detail: Walk or cycle between Thai, Myanmar, Chinese, and German temples — each architecturally different.
atDestination.fact: More than twenty nations built temples here — a rare open-air museum of Buddhist architecture.

atDestination.name: Sunauli border day trip
atDestination.detail: India crossing at Sunauli is 30 min south. Useful if you continue overland — carry passport and visa.
atDestination.fact: Sunauli is one of the busiest Nepal–India crossings — pilgrims and traders share the same Terai road.

modes.name: Direct / express bus
modes.from: Pokhara tourist bus park or Lakeside pickup
modes.detail: Daily services on the Siddhartha Highway in season. One long day — winding hills then Terai heat. Reclining seats on better lines.
extras: Taxi to Maya Devi zone NPR 200–400
modes.goodFor: Pilgrims, budget, Pokhara–Lumbini without backtracking via KTM

modes.name: Private car / jeep
modes.detail: Stop at Tansen for lunch and views if you want. AC helps on the Terai approach. Best for 2–4 travellers with bags.
modes.goodFor: Families, Tansen detour, pace control

modes.name: Via Kathmandu (two hops)
modes.price: Sum of KTM legs or flights
modes.detail: Some travellers fly PKR–KTM and KTM–Bhairahawa instead of the Siddhartha road. Costs more but skips the long hill highway. See Kathmandu → Lumbini and Kathmandu → Pokhara hops.
modes.goodFor: Flight preference, monsoon when hill roads are slow

notes: Sample 2026 fares. Siddhartha Highway can be slow after rain — build buffer time. Combine with Pokhara → ABC only if you have days to spare; this is a full travel day.

title: Chitwan → Lumbini
summary: Two UNESCO sites in one Terai stretch: leave the rhino lodges, cross the flat plains through Butwal, and reach the Buddha’s birthplace the same day. Shortest hop between jungle and pilgrimage on this map.

alongTheWay.name: Sauraha checkout
alongTheWay.do: Leave after breakfast — aim on the road by 8:00.
alongTheWay.detail: Your lodge arranges the taxi or jeep to the Narayangarh–Butwal highway.
alongTheWay.fact: Many travellers pair Chitwan safari with Lumbini — two UNESCO sites in one Terai week.

alongTheWay.name: Narayangarh bypass
alongTheWay.do: Fuel and tea if the driver stops.
alongTheWay.detail: You may not enter town — through-traffic heads west on the Mahendra Highway.
alongTheWay.fact: The east–west Mahendra Highway links Kakarbhitta on the eastern border to the far west — Lumbini sits on its corridor.

alongTheWay.name: Butwal junction
alongTheWay.do: Last proper town before Bhairahawa and Lumbini.
alongTheWay.detail: Flat, hot, busy. Good place for dal bhat and a toilet break.
alongTheWay.fact: Butwal is where hill roads from Tansen and Tansen meet the Terai grid — a natural rest stop.

alongTheWay.name: Bhairahawa approach
alongTheWay.do: Confirm whether your bus stops at bazaar or Bhairahawa airport road.
alongTheWay.detail: The sacred garden is west of town — not walkable with bags in midday heat.
alongTheWay.fact: Bhairahawa’s airport code BWA is how many international pilgrims first land for Lumbini.

alongTheWay.name: Lumbini monastic zone
alongTheWay.do: Check in, rest from the heat, Maya Devi at dusk or dawn tomorrow.
alongTheWay.detail: Flat and contemplative — opposite energy to a jeep safari. Plan slow walks and shade.
alongTheWay.fact: The eternal peace flame has burned since 1986 — pilgrims light butter lamps beside it at evening.

atDestination.name: Maya Devi garden
atDestination.detail: The core pilgrimage site — quieter early morning before tour groups arrive.
atDestination.fact: The Ashoka pillar still marks the spot Emperor Ashoka identified in the 3rd century BCE.

atDestination.name: World Peace Pagoda
atDestination.detail: Cycle or rickshaw from the canal. Calm views over the Terai after Chitwan’s jungle intensity.
atDestination.fact: Japanese donors funded this stupa as part of a global peace-pagoda network spanning eighty sites.

atDestination.name: Crane sanctuary walk
atDestination.detail: Birdlife and wetlands — a gentler morning after early Chitwan safaris.
atDestination.fact: Sarus cranes nest in Lumbini’s fields — the tallest flying bird, revered in Buddhist imagery.

modes.name: Express bus
modes.from: Sauraha pickup or Narayangarh bus park
modes.detail: Through-coaches on the Terai corridor in season. Lodge can book the night before. Mostly flat — easier than the hill highways.
modes.goodFor: Safari + pilgrimage combo, budget Terai crossing

modes.name: Private car / jeep
modes.detail: Straight Terai run with AC. Stop in Butwal for lunch. Fastest way to link two UNESCO sites in one day.
modes.goodFor: 2–4 people, same-day transfer, families

modes.name: Taxi to Bharatpur + flight
modes.detail: Rarely worth it unless you hate road travel — taxi to Bharatpur airport, fly to Bhairahawa (if schedule exists), taxi to Lumbini. Often simpler to drive the Terai flat.
extras: Schedule gaps may force overnight Bharatpur
modes.goodFor: Mobility issues, extreme heat days

notes: Sample 2026 fares. Classic two-week loop: Kathmandu → Chitwan → Lumbini → Pokhara (or Chitwan → Lumbini → Pokhara via backtracking). Terai heat peaks March–June — travel early.

title: Kathmandu → Everest Base Camp
distance: Fly to Lukla (2,860 m) · then ~65 km walking each way to 5,364 m
duration: 12 – 14 days return typical · 4–5 hrs by heli tour
bestSeason: October–November · March–May · avoid monsoon and deep winter
summary: The world’s most famous trek. Fly into Lukla’s cliff-edge runway, then walk up the Dudh Koshi through Namche Bazaar, Tengboche, and Dingboche to the Khumbu glacier. Two acclimatisation days are not optional. No road touches this hop — everything above Lukla moves on foot, yak, or helicopter.

alongTheWay.name: Ramechhap (Manthali) airstrip
alongTheWay.do: Sleep in the jeep, then queue for the first Lukla flights at dawn.
alongTheWay.detail: In October–November and March–May most Lukla flights leave from Manthali, not Kathmandu, to ease TIA congestion. Some trekkers sleep in Manthali the night before instead of the midnight drive.
alongTheWay.fact: Manthali sits at only 470 m — the Lukla flight from here climbs almost 2,400 m in 20 minutes.

alongTheWay.name: Lukla · Tenzing-Hillary Airport
alongTheWay.duration: Chiya, then 3–4 hrs walk to Phakding
alongTheWay.do: Meet your porter, check bags, walk down to Phakding for the first night.
alongTheWay.detail: Do not sleep in Lukla unless weather strands you. The first day descends — a gentle start that helps the body.
alongTheWay.fact: Lukla’s runway is 527 m long on a 12 % slope with a mountain at one end and a 600 m drop at the other — routinely called the most dangerous airport in the world.

alongTheWay.name: Namche Bazaar
alongTheWay.do: Saturday market, Sherpa Culture Museum, day hike to Everest View Hotel or Khumjung.
alongTheWay.detail: The Sherpa capital and the last place with ATMs, bakeries, and gear shops. Sagarmatha National Park entry is checked at Monjo just below.
alongTheWay.fact: The Everest View Hotel above Namche (3,880 m) was the highest hotel in the world when it opened in 1971 — guests once arrived by plane at Syangboche with oxygen in their rooms.

alongTheWay.name: Tengboche monastery
alongTheWay.cost: Lodge NPR 800–2,500 · donation at the gompa
alongTheWay.do: Afternoon puja at 3:00 pm, Ama Dablam at sunset.
alongTheWay.detail: The spiritual centre of the Khumbu on a ridge with Everest, Lhotse, and Ama Dablam in one frame. Cold nights start here.
alongTheWay.fact: Tengboche hosts the Mani Rimdu festival every October–November — masked dances that draw Sherpas from every village in the Khumbu.

alongTheWay.name: Dingboche & Lobuche
alongTheWay.cost: Lodge NPR 1,000–3,000 · meals climb to NPR 1,200–2,000
alongTheWay.do: Nangkartshang hike (5,083 m) from Dingboche, then Thukla pass memorials, then Lobuche.
alongTheWay.detail: This is where altitude bites. Sleep low, walk high, drink 3–4 litres. Thukla’s stone memorials to climbers are the sobering midpoint.
alongTheWay.fact: The Thukla pass memorials include cairns for Scott Fischer and Babu Chiri Sherpa — Babu once slept on Everest’s summit for 21 hours without oxygen.

alongTheWay.name: Gorak Shep
alongTheWay.duration: 3 hrs from Lobuche, then 2–3 hrs return to EBC
alongTheWay.cost: Lodge NPR 1,500–3,500 · dorm beds in peak season
alongTheWay.do: Drop bags, walk to base camp the same afternoon, Kala Patthar at dawn.
alongTheWay.detail: The last lodges on a frozen lakebed. Cold, crowded, and unforgettable. Nobody sleeps well here — that is normal.
alongTheWay.fact: Gorak Shep was the original Everest base camp for the 1952 Swiss expedition — the modern camp is an hour further up the glacier.

atDestination.name: Everest Base Camp
atDestination.time: 2–3 hours return from Gorak Shep · 5,364 m
atDestination.detail: Prayer flags, the Khumbu icefall, and in April–May the tents of summit expeditions. Everest itself hides behind Nuptse from here.
atDestination.fact: Base camp moves every year with the glacier — the Khumbu ice beneath it flows downhill about a metre a day.

atDestination.name: Kala Patthar sunrise
atDestination.price: Free — bring every layer you own
atDestination.detail: The only place on this trek where Everest’s summit is fully visible. Leave Gorak Shep at 4:30 am with a headtorch; it is often −15 °C.
atDestination.fact: Kala Patthar is where the Nepal government held a cabinet meeting in 2009 to highlight climate change — the highest cabinet meeting ever recorded.

atDestination.name: Helicopter out
atDestination.time: 15–20 min to Lukla · 45 min to Kathmandu
atDestination.price: US$500–900 pp shared to Lukla · US$1,800–3,500 charter to KTM
atDestination.detail: Weather window only. Many trekkers fly out from Gorak Shep or Pheriche to save three walking days. Book through your guide or the Pokhara/Kathmandu heli companies.
atDestination.fact: Heli traffic in the Khumbu now exceeds fixed-wing flights — over 40,000 helicopter movements a year, most in the two trekking seasons.

atDestination.name: Khumjung & Khunde on the descent
atDestination.price: Lodge + food as on the way up
atDestination.detail: Walk the quieter villages above Namche — Hillary’s school, the Khumjung gompa, and a rest before the Lukla flight.
atDestination.fact: Khumjung monastery keeps what it says is a yeti scalp in a locked box — Edmund Hillary flew it to Chicago in 1960 for testing.

modes.name: Fly to Lukla, then trek
modes.price: Flight NPR 24,000 – 31,000 pp one way (foreigner) + trail NPR 8,000 – 15,000 / day
modes.from: Kathmandu (TIA) off-season · Ramechhap/Manthali in peak season
modes.to: Lukla, then on foot to EBC
modes.detail: Tara Air, Summit Air, and Sita Air fly Twin Otters and Dorniers at dawn only. Fog, wind, and cloud cancel often — build two buffer days at the end. Nepali citizens pay a much lower fare.
extras: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality fee NPR 3,000
Ramechhap jeep NPR 2,500–4,000 in peak season
modes.goodFor: Everyone who has 14 days — this is the standard EBC shape

modes.name: Guided EBC package
modes.detail: Licensed guide, Lukla flights both ways, permits, lodges, and usually three meals a day on the trail. Porters are shared one per two trekkers. Ask whether Ramechhap transfers, hot showers, Wi-Fi, charging, and a Kathmandu hotel night are included. Sample 14-day shape: Lukla–Phakding–Namche (2)–Tengboche–Dingboche (2)–Lobuche–Gorak Shep/EBC–Kala Patthar–Pheriche–Namche–Lukla.
extras: Tips — budget US$150–250 per trekker for guide and porter
Travel insurance covering heli evacuation to 6,000 m (mandatory in practice)
Sleeping bag and down jacket rental NPR 300–500 / day
modes.goodFor: First Himalayan trek, fixed dates, international visitors

modes.name: Independent trek + day rates
modes.duration: You set the days · 12 minimum recommended
modes.detail: Lodges NPR 500–3,000 if you eat there. Dal bhat rises from NPR 600 in Phakding to NPR 1,500+ at Gorak Shep; a hot shower or charging costs NPR 500–1,000 high up. The Khumbu still admits independent trekkers — check the current guide rule before you go. Carry all cash from Namche.
includes: You book lodges as you go
extras: Guide NPR 3,500–5,000 / day · porter NPR 2,500–3,500 / day if hired in Lukla
Sagarmatha NP NPR 3,000 + Khumbu municipality NPR 3,000 (foreigners)
modes.goodFor: Experienced trekkers, Nepali groups, open schedules

modes.name: Jeep to Salleri / Thamdanda, then walk in
modes.duration: 10 – 14 hrs jeep + 2–3 extra walking days each way
modes.to: Salleri or the Thamdanda / Surke road-end, then walk to Lukla and beyond
modes.detail: Skips Lukla’s weather roulette. The road now reaches Surke below Lukla in dry season. Adds days and a brutal drive but saves money and works when flights are cancelled for a week.
extras: Extra lodge nights on the lower trail
Same permits as the flight route
modes.goodFor: Budget, flight anxiety, extra acclimatisation, monsoon shoulder

modes.name: Everest helicopter tour
modes.to: Kala Patthar landing + breakfast at Everest View Hotel, back to KTM
modes.detail: Dawn departure, refuel at Lukla, 10-minute landing at Kala Patthar (5,545 m) for photos, then breakfast at Syangboche. Weather cancels; rebook the next morning. No acclimatisation — you are exposed to altitude briefly and then descend.
includes: Flight, Lukla refuel stop, Kala Patthar landing
extras: Sagarmatha NP fee usually built into the price — confirm
modes.goodFor: Half a day, elderly travellers, seeing Everest without walking

notes: Sample 2026 fares. Foreigner fares on Lukla flights are fixed in USD and rise yearly. Altitude sickness is the real risk — walk slowly above Namche, never climb more than 500 m of sleeping altitude per day, and descend at once if symptoms worsen. Insurance with helicopter evacuation is essential. Keep two spare days for Lukla weather before any international flight.

title: Pokhara → Poon Hill
distance: Trailhead 1.5–3 hrs by road · then a 3–5 day walking loop to 3,210 m
bestSeason: October–November · March–April for rhododendrons · fine in winter with clear skies
summary: Nepal’s most popular short trek and the classic first Himalayan walk. A jeep to Nayapul or Ulleri, one hard day of stone stairs, a night in Ghorepani, and a pre-dawn climb to the Poon Hill view tower for Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, and Machhapuchhre in one sweep. Loop back through Tadapani and Ghandruk — or keep walking to ABC.

alongTheWay.name: Nayapul / Birethanti
alongTheWay.do: ACAP and TIMS check, then walk the Bhurungdi Khola to Tikhedhunga.
alongTheWay.detail: Same gate as the ABC hop. The Poon Hill loop turns north here toward Ulleri instead of east toward Ghandruk.
alongTheWay.fact: Birethanti’s ACAP checkpoint logs more than 100,000 trekkers a year — most of them heading for Poon Hill.

alongTheWay.name: Tikhedhunga & the Ulleri stairs
alongTheWay.do: Climb the famous 3,300 steps to Ulleri — or jeep to Ulleri and skip them.
alongTheWay.detail: The stairs are the hardest hour of the trek and the reason people remember it. A dirt road now reaches Ulleri; shared jeeps from Pokhara stop here.
alongTheWay.fact: The Ulleri staircase has roughly 3,300 stone steps laid by Magar villagers — locals still carry loads up it every day.

alongTheWay.name: Ghorepani
alongTheWay.duration: 4–5 hrs from Ulleri through rhododendron forest
alongTheWay.do: Warm up by the stove, set an alarm for 4:30 am, book a headtorch and hot tea.
alongTheWay.detail: A village built for the sunrise walk. Upper Ghorepani has the best lodges and its own mountain view if you cannot face the pre-dawn climb.
alongTheWay.fact: Ghorepani means “horse water” — the village grew as a watering stop for mule caravans on the old salt route to Mustang.

alongTheWay.name: Tadapani
alongTheWay.duration: 5–6 hrs from Ghorepani over Deurali pass
alongTheWay.do: Ridge walk with Fishtail straight ahead, then drop into the forest to Tadapani.
alongTheWay.detail: The quietest day of the loop. Langur monkeys, rhododendron, and Annapurna South filling the sky at the lodge.
alongTheWay.fact: Tadapani’s name means “far water” — until a pipe was laid, villagers walked an hour each way to fetch it.

alongTheWay.name: Ghandruk
alongTheWay.do: Gurung Museum, stone lanes, a last Machhapuchhre sunset.
alongTheWay.detail: From Ghandruk a jeep road runs back to Pokhara in 3 hours, or continue on foot toward Chhomrong and ABC.
alongTheWay.fact: Ghandruk supplied more Gurkha soldiers to the British and Indian armies than almost any other village in Nepal — pensions built its stone houses.

atDestination.name: Poon Hill sunrise
atDestination.time: Dawn · 3,210 m · 45–60 min climb from Ghorepani
atDestination.price: View tower fee NPR 100–150 · tea at the top NPR 150–250
atDestination.detail: Dhaulagiri (8,167 m), Tukuche, Nilgiri, Annapurna I (8,091 m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre. Go early — 200–400 people share the hill in October.
atDestination.fact: Poon Hill is the only spot in Nepal where two 8,000 m peaks — Dhaulagiri and Annapurna I — stand side by side across the deepest gorge on Earth.

atDestination.name: Rhododendron forest
atDestination.detail: Late March to mid-April the forest turns red, pink, and white. Nepal’s national flower — laligurans — at its best.
atDestination.fact: Some rhododendron trees on this ridge are over 20 m tall — the tallest of any rhododendron species in the world.

atDestination.name: Extend to ABC
atDestination.detail: From Tadapani or Ghandruk walk to Chhomrong and join the sanctuary trail. Same permits, one longer trek.
atDestination.fact: Poon Hill plus ABC is the most-walked combination in the Annapurna region — about ten days for both.

atDestination.name: Jhinu Danda hot springs
atDestination.detail: From Ghandruk drop to the Modi Khola for the natural pools, then jeep from New Bridge back to Pokhara.
atDestination.fact: The Jhinu pools sit at about 1,780 m beside the river — the perfect cure for Ulleri’s stairs.

modes.name: Jeep to Nayapul, then walk the full loop
modes.from: Lakeside or Baglung bus park, Pokhara
modes.to: Nayapul, then on foot Ulleri → Ghorepani → Poon Hill → Tadapani → Ghandruk
modes.detail: The standard shape. Shared jeeps leave Baglung bus park from 6:00 am. Day 1 Nayapul–Ulleri or Tikhedhunga, Day 2 Ghorepani, Day 3 Poon Hill–Tadapani, Day 4 Ghandruk–Pokhara.
extras: Jeep Ghandruk or Kimche → Pokhara NPR 600–1,000 shared
modes.goodFor: Full loop, villages, first-time trekkers

modes.name: Jeep to Ulleri or Hile, shorter walk
modes.detail: The dirt road climbs above the Ulleri staircase. Sleep Ghorepani the first night, Poon Hill the next dawn, then down via Ghandruk or back the same way. Road closes in heavy monsoon.
modes.goodFor: Weekend from Pokhara, knees, limited days

modes.name: Guided Poon Hill package
modes.to: Poon Hill loop and back to Pokhara
modes.detail: Guide, permits, lodges, jeep transfers, and often meals. Cheapest guided Himalayan trek in Nepal. Confirm whether a porter and the view-tower fee are included.
modes.goodFor: Families, first trek, solo travellers who want company

modes.name: Independent trek + day rates
modes.detail: Lodges NPR 500–2,000, dal bhat NPR 500–900, hot shower NPR 200–400. The trail is well marked and busy — the easiest trek in Nepal to walk alone. Check current guide rules for the Annapurna region; enforcement varies.
includes: You book lodges as you go
modes.goodFor: Budget, Nepali groups, flexible dates

notes: Sample 2026 fares. Poon Hill is under 3,300 m — altitude is rarely an issue, but Ulleri’s stairs and the pre-dawn climb are real. Bring a headtorch, warm layers for the summit wait (often 0–5 °C), and cash — no ATMs after Pokhara. Rhododendrons peak late March to mid-April.

title: Pokhara → Jomsom & Muktinath
distance: 160 km · Beni–Jomsom road up the Kali Gandaki gorge · or 20 min by air
duration: 20 min flight · 8 – 10 hours by jeep or bus
bestSeason: October–November · March–May · in the Himalayan rain shadow, so June–August works too
summary: Fly twenty minutes over the deepest gorge on Earth, or spend a day grinding up the Kali Gandaki road, and arrive in a windswept high desert that feels like Tibet. Jomsom is the hub; Marpha, Kagbeni, and the Muktinath temple at 3,710 m are the reasons to come. No restricted permit needed below Kagbeni.

alongTheWay.name: Beni
alongTheWay.when: ~3 hrs from Pokhara · end of the tarmac
alongTheWay.do: Change to a jeep if you came by bus; stock up on water.
alongTheWay.detail: The Kali Gandaki road begins here. Beyond Beni it is rough, dusty, and spectacular — high-clearance vehicles only.
alongTheWay.fact: Beni sits where the Myagdi Khola meets the Kali Gandaki — the town was the site of a major 2004 battle during Nepal’s civil war.

alongTheWay.name: Tatopani hot springs
alongTheWay.duration: 1–2 hrs at the pools · or overnight
alongTheWay.do: Soak in the riverside pools, sleep here if you split the drive.
alongTheWay.detail: The classic break on the two-day jeep version. Below the gorge, warm, and still subtropical — oranges grow here.
alongTheWay.fact: Tatopani literally means “hot water” — the springs were a rest stop on the Annapurna Circuit long before the road arrived.

alongTheWay.name: Ghasa & the Kali Gandaki gorge
alongTheWay.do: Look up: Dhaulagiri on one side, Annapurna I on the other.
alongTheWay.detail: The road threads the narrowest section of the gorge. Landslides close it for hours after rain — the driver knows.
alongTheWay.fact: Between Dhaulagiri (8,167 m) and Annapurna I (8,091 m) the Kali Gandaki gorge drops more than 5,500 m from peak to river — the deepest gorge on Earth by that measure.

alongTheWay.name: Marpha
alongTheWay.cost: Lodge NPR 800–2,500 · apple brandy NPR 300–600 a bottle
alongTheWay.do: Whitewashed Thakali lanes, apple orchards, the gompa above town.
alongTheWay.detail: The prettiest village on the road. Many travellers sleep here instead of Jomsom.
alongTheWay.fact: Marpha’s apples came from a 1966 government horticulture farm — now the village is known across Nepal for dried apples, cider, and brandy.

alongTheWay.name: Jomsom
alongTheWay.do: Airport, ACAP checkpost, jeeps to Muktinath and Kagbeni, Mustang Eco Museum.
alongTheWay.detail: Windy after 11:00 am every day — flights only run at dawn. Bank, ATMs, and the last real bakery before Upper Mustang.
alongTheWay.fact: Jomsom’s afternoon wind is a daily thermal — air rushing up the gorge from the lowlands, strong enough to sandblast your face and ground every plane.

alongTheWay.name: Kagbeni
alongTheWay.do: Mud-brick alleys, the red gompa, and the checkpost gate to Upper Mustang.
alongTheWay.detail: Walk the alleys and the riverbank; Tiri village across the river is a quiet extra hour. Beyond the checkpost you need the US$500 restricted permit.
alongTheWay.fact: Kagbeni’s 15th-century Kag Chode monastery once controlled the salt trade — every caravan between Tibet and India paid tax here.

atDestination.name: Muktinath temple
atDestination.time: Half day · 3,710 m · 1.5 hrs jeep from Jomsom
atDestination.price: Jeep NPR 600–900 shared · NPR 5,000–7,000 private · temple free
atDestination.detail: Walk from Ranipauwa through the 108 water spouts, the Jwala Mai eternal flame, and the Buddhist gompa. Hindus and Buddhists share the same courtyard.
atDestination.fact: Muktinath is one of the world’s highest major pilgrimage sites — Hindu pilgrims bathe under all 108 spouts of glacial water in a single freezing pass for moksha.

atDestination.name: Kagbeni & Tiri
atDestination.detail: Mud walls, prayer wheels, and the Kali Gandaki riverbed where shaligram fossils are found.
atDestination.fact: Shaligram — black ammonite fossils sacred to Vishnu — are found only in the Kali Gandaki, proof that this desert was once an ocean floor.

atDestination.name: Marpha apple walk
atDestination.detail: Walk or jeep from Jomsom, tour an orchard, eat apple pie at a Thakali kitchen, buy dried apple for the trail.
atDestination.fact: Marpha produces most of Nepal’s apple brandy — the distillery was set up with Swiss help in the 1970s.

atDestination.name: Lubra & Jhong side valleys
atDestination.detail: Lubra is a Bön village, Jhong has a ruined fort — both quiet alternatives to the Muktinath crowds.
atDestination.fact: Lubra is one of the last villages in Nepal that follows Bön — the pre-Buddhist religion of Tibet.

modes.name: Flight Pokhara → Jomsom
modes.to: Jomsom airport, then jeep to Kagbeni or Muktinath
modes.detail: Tara Air and Summit Air fly Twin Otters between 6:30 and 10:00 am — after that the gorge wind grounds everything. Sit on the left going up for Dhaulagiri. Cancellations are common; keep a road backup.
modes.goodFor: Short time, gorge views from the air, elderly pilgrims

modes.name: Public bus or shared jeep
modes.detail: Buses leave 6:00–7:00 am and grind the whole way; shared jeeps are faster and change at Beni. Rough, dusty, spectacular. Bring a mask and a sense of humour.
modes.goodFor: Budget travellers, Nepali pilgrims, no-flight preference

modes.name: Private jeep, two days via Tatopani
modes.duration: 2 days with a Tatopani or Marpha night
modes.to: Jomsom, Kagbeni, or straight to Muktinath
modes.detail: The comfortable version. Stop for hot springs, the gorge, Marpha lunch, and photos. The jeep can stay with you for Muktinath and Kagbeni days at NPR 8,000–12,000 / day.
extras: Keep the jeep in Mustang NPR 8,000–12,000 / day
modes.goodFor: Families, pilgrimage groups, photographers

modes.name: Guided Lower Mustang package
modes.to: Jomsom, Kagbeni, Muktinath, Marpha and back
modes.detail: Flight or jeep, guide, ACAP, lodges, and local jeeps. Some packages walk Jomsom–Kagbeni–Muktinath (2 days) and fly back. Upper Mustang (Lo Manthang) is a separate 10-day restricted-area trek at US$500 for the permit alone.
extras: Upper Mustang permit US$500 / 10 days if you go beyond Kagbeni
modes.goodFor: First visit, mixed pilgrimage and trekking, fixed dates

notes: Sample 2026 fares. Lower Mustang (Jomsom, Marpha, Kagbeni, Muktinath) needs only the ACAP permit; anything north of the Kagbeni checkpost is Upper Mustang and needs the restricted-area permit and a registered guide. Muktinath is 3,710 m — flying straight from Pokhara (822 m) and driving up the same day gives many people headaches. Sleep in Jomsom or Kagbeni first. Afternoon wind is fierce; carry sunglasses, a buff, and lip balm.

title: Kathmandu → Langtang Valley
distance: 120 km road to Syabrubesi · then ~35 km walking up to Kyanjin Gompa (3,870 m)
bestSeason: October–November · March–May · clear cold winters possible
summary: The Himalayan valley closest to Kathmandu and the third most-walked trek in Nepal. One long bus day north to Syabrubesi, then three days up a forested gorge to a rebuilt Tamang village and Kyanjin Gompa under Langtang Lirung. Quieter than Everest or Annapurna, with two summit ridges above 4,700 m and a cheese factory at the top.

alongTheWay.name: Trishuli Bazaar
alongTheWay.do: Dal bhat, toilet, stretch — the road gets rough after this.
alongTheWay.detail: The last flat town. From here the road climbs the Trishuli gorge in switchbacks toward Dhunche.
alongTheWay.fact: The Trishuli river here is the same one rafters ride on the Kathmandu–Pokhara highway — it rises in Tibet and crosses into Nepal at Rasuwagadhi.

alongTheWay.name: Dhunche · Langtang National Park gate
alongTheWay.do: Show or buy the park permit; the army post checks passports.
alongTheWay.detail: Rasuwa district headquarters and the alternative trailhead for Gosaikunda. Most Langtang Valley trekkers continue down to Syabrubesi.
alongTheWay.fact: Langtang was Nepal’s first Himalayan national park (1976) and the second oldest in the country after Chitwan.

alongTheWay.name: Syabrubesi
alongTheWay.do: Sleep, hire a porter if you need one, start walking at 7:00 am.
alongTheWay.detail: The trailhead. A hot spring sits by the river below town. The China border at Rasuwagadhi is 15 km north.
alongTheWay.fact: Syabrubesi is on the ancient Kyirong trade route — Tamang villagers here traded salt and wool with Tibet for centuries.

alongTheWay.name: Lama Hotel
alongTheWay.do: Watch for langurs and red pandas; sleep in the forest clearing.
alongTheWay.detail: A cluster of lodges, not a village. The trail follows the Langtang Khola through bamboo and oak. Leeches in monsoon.
alongTheWay.fact: Langtang National Park is one of the best places in Nepal to see red pandas — the bamboo forest between Bamboo and Lama Hotel is their habitat.

alongTheWay.name: Langtang village
alongTheWay.do: Visit the memorial, stay in the rebuilt village, walk slowly — this is where altitude starts.
alongTheWay.detail: The 2015 earthquake avalanche buried the old village. New Langtang sits just above; the mani wall memorial lists 243 names.
alongTheWay.fact: The Langtang avalanche released the energy of about half the Hiroshima bomb — the air blast alone flattened forest across the valley.

alongTheWay.name: Kyanjin Gompa
alongTheWay.do: Monastery, cheese factory, then a rest day for the ridge climbs.
alongTheWay.detail: The last village. Glaciers on three sides and Langtang Lirung (7,227 m) straight above. Stay two nights.
alongTheWay.fact: Kyanjin’s cheese factory was built in 1955 by Swiss aid worker Werner Schulthess — the first yak cheese made in Nepal, still sold by the kilo.

atDestination.name: Kyanjin Ri
atDestination.detail: 2–3 hrs up from the village for Langtang Lirung, the Lirung glacier, and the whole valley. Start at dawn before cloud builds.
atDestination.fact: Kyanjin Ri’s prayer-flag summit sits directly across from Langtang Lirung — a 3,300 m wall of ice less than 5 km away.

atDestination.name: Tserko Ri
atDestination.price: Free — pack lunch from the lodge
atDestination.detail: The bigger climb: 4–5 hrs up for Shishapangma (8,027 m) in Tibet, Langshisa Ri, and the Langtang glacier. Leave at 4:00 am.
atDestination.fact: From Tserko Ri you can see Shishapangma — the only 8,000 m peak entirely inside Tibet — over the border ridge.

atDestination.name: Langshisa Kharka glacier walk
atDestination.detail: Flat valley walk east from Kyanjin to yak pastures and the glacier snout. Easier on the lungs than the ridges.
atDestination.fact: Langshisa Kharka is where Tilman and his 1949 expedition camped — the first Westerners allowed into Langtang.

atDestination.name: Gosaikunda extension
atDestination.time: +3–4 days via Thulo Syabru and Lauribina pass
atDestination.detail: Descend to Thulo Syabru, climb to the sacred lakes at 4,380 m, cross the Lauribina La (4,610 m), and walk out to Sundarijal at the edge of Kathmandu.
atDestination.fact: Gosaikunda draws tens of thousands of Hindu pilgrims every August full moon — Shiva is said to have created the lake with his trident.

modes.name: Local bus to Syabrubesi
modes.detail: Buses leave 6:30–8:00 am. Rough, crowded, and slow through the Trishuli gorge switchbacks. Buy tickets the day before in season; sit on the right for views.
extras: Langtang NP permit NPR 3,000 at Dhunche or Kathmandu
modes.goodFor: Tight budgets, the real road

modes.name: Shared jeep
modes.detail: Faster and less crowded than the bus. 8–10 seats; books out in October. Ask your Thamel agency or the Machhapokhari counters.
modes.goodFor: Most independent trekkers

modes.name: Private jeep
modes.detail: Leave at 6:00 am, stop where you like. Worth splitting between 4–6 trekkers. Book the return for your exit day.
modes.goodFor: Groups, families, bad-road aversion

modes.name: Guided Langtang package
modes.detail: Guide, permits, transport, lodges, and usually meals. A licensed guide is required inside Langtang National Park under the 2023 rule — check enforcement, but plan for one. Gosaikunda add-on usually +US$200–300.
modes.goodFor: First trek, solo travellers, fixed dates

modes.name: Independent day rates on the trail
modes.duration: You set the days · 6 walking days minimum
modes.detail: Lodges NPR 500–3,000, dal bhat NPR 500–1,200, hot shower NPR 300–600. Cash only after Syabrubesi. Kyanjin has bakeries and yak cheese — budget a little extra for both.
includes: You book lodges as you go
modes.goodFor: Experienced walkers, Nepali groups

notes: Sample 2026 fares. Kyanjin Gompa is 3,870 m and the ridges near 5,000 m — take a rest day at Kyanjin before climbing. The Syabrubesi road is landslide-prone in monsoon and closes for hours after heavy rain. Spend your money in Langtang village — the rebuilt lodges are the valley’s recovery.

title: Kathmandu → Nagarkot
distance: 32 km · east through Bhaktapur, then a 2,175 m ridge road
duration: 1.5 – 2.5 hours by road · 3–4 hrs if you hike from Changu Narayan
bestSeason: October–December · February–April · clearest mountain mornings after monsoon
summary: The easiest famous hop in Nepal and the classic first or last night of a trip. Leave the city, spend the afternoon in Bhaktapur’s medieval squares, climb to the valley rim for a sunset, and wake up to a Himalayan panorama from Langtang to — on a very clear day — a tiny tip of Everest. Bus, taxi, bicycle, or on foot.

alongTheWay.name: Thimi (Madhyapur)
alongTheWay.do: Watch potters throw clay in the squares; buy a small piece.
alongTheWay.detail: A Newari pottery town most travellers pass without noticing. Worth a stop in a private car.
alongTheWay.fact: Thimi hosts the Bisket Jatra ‘sindoor’ festival every April — 32 palanquins and clouds of orange powder in one square.

alongTheWay.name: Bhaktapur Durbar Square
alongTheWay.cost: Entry NPR 1,800 (foreigner) · NPR 500 (SAARC) · free for Nepalis
alongTheWay.do: 55-Window Palace, Nyatapola temple, Taumadhi and Dattatreya squares, juju dhau.
alongTheWay.detail: The best-preserved of the three valley kingdoms. Give it real time — the lanes between the squares are the point. Your ticket is valid for repeat visits if you show it.
alongTheWay.fact: Nyatapola, Nepal’s tallest pagoda at 30 m, was built in 1702 and survived both the 1934 and 2015 earthquakes almost untouched.

alongTheWay.name: Changu Narayan
alongTheWay.when: Optional detour or hike start · 1,540 m
alongTheWay.duration: 1 hr visit · 2.5–3 hrs hike to Nagarkot
alongTheWay.do: See the oldest temple in the valley, then walk the ridge trail to Nagarkot.
alongTheWay.detail: A UNESCO site on a hilltop north of Bhaktapur. The trail to Nagarkot climbs through pine forest and villages — clear, mostly uphill, no guide needed.
alongTheWay.fact: Changu Narayan has a stone inscription from AD 464 — the oldest dated inscription in Nepal.

alongTheWay.name: Telkot & the ridge road
alongTheWay.do: Look back over the whole valley as the road climbs.
alongTheWay.detail: Buses from Bhaktapur’s Kamalbinayak stop labour up here. Taxis take 30–40 minutes from Bhaktapur.
alongTheWay.fact: Nagarkot was a summer retreat for Kathmandu’s royal court — the name means ‘city fort’, from a lookout that guarded the valley’s eastern edge.

alongTheWay.name: Nagarkot bazaar & hotels
alongTheWay.do: Drop bags, walk to the sunset point, set an alarm for 5:30 am.
alongTheWay.detail: Hotels line the ridge for 2 km. The view tower is 4 km south — a taxi or an early walk. Cold at night even in October.
alongTheWay.fact: On the clearest winter mornings Nagarkot shows eight of Nepal’s fourteen Himalayan ranges — including a tiny Everest on the far eastern horizon.

atDestination.name: Sunrise from the view tower
atDestination.time: Dawn · 2,195 m · 4 km from the bazaar
atDestination.detail: Langtang, Ganesh Himal, Manaslu, and on a clear morning the Everest range far to the east. Arrive 20 minutes before sunrise; cloud fills in fast.
atDestination.fact: The view tower sits on the old Nepal Army lookout — the panorama covers roughly 250 km of Himalaya from Annapurna to Everest.

atDestination.name: Nagarkot → Changu Narayan hike
atDestination.detail: The reverse of the classic hike — walk down through villages to the temple, then bus or taxi to Bhaktapur. The best way to leave.
atDestination.fact: The ridge trail passes Tamang and Newari villages that still terrace millet and mustard on the valley rim.

atDestination.name: Nagarkot → Dhulikhel ridge walk
atDestination.detail: Longer and quieter — follow the ridge east through Rohini Bhanjyang to Dhulikhel, then bus back to Kathmandu on the Araniko Highway.
atDestination.fact: Dhulikhel marks the start of the Araniko Highway to Tibet — the ridge you walk was the old Kathmandu–Lhasa trade path.

atDestination.name: Back to Bhaktapur for juju dhau
atDestination.detail: ‘King curd’ in a clay pot, then Pottery Square before the bus back to the city.
atDestination.fact: Juju dhau is set in unglazed clay pots that wick moisture out — the same technique Bhaktapur has used for 500 years.

modes.name: Local bus via Bhaktapur
modes.detail: Buses to Bhaktapur run every few minutes. From Kamalbinayak, Nagarkot buses leave every 30–60 min until about 5:00 pm. Slow, cheap, and easy.
extras: Bhaktapur entry NPR 1,800 if you walk through the squares
modes.goodFor: Budget travellers, stopping in Bhaktapur

modes.name: Taxi
modes.price: NPR 2,500 – 4,000 one way · NPR 5,000 – 7,000 return with sunrise wait
modes.detail: Agree the price before you leave. Add NPR 500–1,000 for a Bhaktapur stop of an hour or two. Ride-hailing apps work to Bhaktapur but rarely up the ridge.
extras: View tower run at dawn NPR 500–1,000
modes.goodFor: Couples, luggage, arriving before sunset

modes.name: Private car day tour with Bhaktapur
modes.to: Bhaktapur, Changu Narayan, Nagarkot and back
modes.detail: Driver waits at each stop. Overnight versions collect you after sunrise the next morning. Add a guide for Bhaktapur at NPR 2,000–3,500.
modes.goodFor: Families, first day in Nepal, jet-lag recovery

modes.name: Hike from Changu Narayan or mountain bike
modes.duration: 3 hrs hiking · 3–4 hrs cycling from Kathmandu
modes.price: Free on foot · bike rental NPR 1,500 – 3,000 / day
modes.from: Changu Narayan (bus/taxi from Bhaktapur) or Thamel bike shops
modes.detail: The hike is the classic: taxi to Changu Narayan (NPR 800–1,200 from Bhaktapur), then a clear ridge trail up. Cyclists take the Bhaktapur road and the 20 km climb; the descent to Sankhu or Dhulikhel the next day is the reward.
modes.goodFor: Acclimatising before a trek, cyclists, a Nepal day walk with no permits

notes: Sample 2026 fares. Nagarkot is about weather: October–December and February–April give the clearest mornings; monsoon (June–September) hides the mountains almost every day. Nights on the ridge are 5–10 °C colder than Kathmandu. Bhaktapur’s NPR 1,800 entry ticket can be extended free for the length of your visa if you ask at the counter with your passport.
